key_idea: Each operation preserves (#black - #white), and the target has difference 0, so the answer is simply whether the counts are equal.
sketch: Replacing a segment with one more black than white by a single black stone removes equally many of each colour, so the difference B-W is invariant; the final state B=W=1 needs B==W. Conversely with equal counts on a circle you can always find an adjacent BW pair with a neighbour to shrink (e.g. BWB -> B) until two stones remain. Count the letters and print 1 or 0, O(n).
